name: Avalon
summary: Hidden loyalty game where Good tries to pass three Quests while Evil infiltrates teams, sabotages, and hunts Merlin.
rules_text: 5-10 players are secretly dealt Good or Evil roles, one Good is Merlin who knows Evil, one Evil is Assassin. Each of 5 rounds a Leader proposes a team size per table and players discuss. All vote Approve/Reject simultaneously; majority approves or team fails. If 5 teams are rejected in one round Evil wins. Approved team members secretly play Success (Good must play Success) or Fail; cards are shuffled and revealed. Usually one Fail fails the Quest, but 4th Quest with 7+ players needs two Fails. First to 3 Successes or 3 Fails ends game. If Good gets 3 Successes, Evil may assassinate one player; if they kill Merlin Evil wins, else Good wins.
rating_reason: Avalon hidden loyalty social deduction, voting, perfect for engine.
reasons: capability: conditional_subsequence: the step list is flat: a whole BLOCK of steps cannot be chosen instead of another block. This is NOT a limit on conditional scoring or conditional updates: a single step can carry a `when` condition and a single operation an `if`, both arithmetic, so 'the poisoner scores if the choices match, otherwise the chooser' is fine
